story.title: Meta’s next VR device isn’t a headset — it’s glasses

facts.text: After a few leaks, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg finally revealed the company's next-generation Meta VR Glasses at its Connect event tonight.
Arriving in Spring 2027, they look like oversized sunglasses (similar to display frames from Xreal and other), paired with an external power and computing pod, like the Apple Vision Pro.
While they're not cheap at $1,300, they're a far cry from the Vision Pro's original $3,500 cost, or its current $3,700 price.

Since these are obviously VR specs, I don't think they'd have the same privacy concerns as Meta's Ray-Ban and Display glasses , but the company has significantly poisoned the idea of wearing anything in public with cameras.
Meta is pitching the VR Glasses as an all-in-one entertainment and productivity device.
It relies on six external cameras for color passthrough and motion tracking, and also has four internal eye-tracking cameras.
Meta's wired computing puck, which looks compact enough to slip in a pocket, holds 12GB of RAM and 128GB of storage (along with a microSD card slot for more content).
And since the Meta VR runs Quest OS, I'm hoping this 3D content storefront eventually heads to the Quest VR headsets.

It likely won't be as immersive as the Frame and other headsets that completely envelop your field of vision, but for most people, it's probably worth losing that to have a device that's just easier to wear.
You won't look like a huge weirdo slipping them on while flying, and since you wear them like glasses, there's little chance they'll mess up your hair as badly as a typical VR headset.
Additionally, it sounds like the company is taking a cue from Apple's Immersive Video Format — Meta says National Geographic will be launching a new app next year with 180-degree 3D Video.
A new "VR Enhanced Cinema" format will let you watch 3D movies with effects that bleed into your real-world space, similar to the way dynamic ambient lighting on TVs makes content more immersive.
That price puts the VR Glasses between Meta’s $599.99 Quest 3 and a high-end VR headset like Apple’s $3,499 Vision Pro, and I think that’s the right way to think about them.

The separate puck connected with a wire contains the guts powering the headset: a Snapdragon Reality Elite processor, 128GB of storage, 12GB of RAM, and the battery, which Meta says will offer up to three hours of media playback, though you can continue using the glasses even while the puck is being charged.
The display is what Meta calls a 5K MicroOLED “Infinite Display.” It has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye at 37 pixels per degree and supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz.
Meta is still planning to develop full VR headsets, the company’s VP of product for VR, Angela Chang, tells The Verge.
Meta is launching new VR hardware: a pair of glasses.

Meta showed me a clip from James Cameron’s Billie Eilish concert film, which was impressive on a huge virtual display, and parts of the most recent NBA Finals, which was filmed on a format called VR180 that provided a 180-degree view of the court.
I also got to watch some of Avengers: Endgame in what Meta characterized as a “VR Enhanced Cinema” experience made in partnership with Disney and Industrial Light & Magic.
Snap’s idea is the augmented reality-focused Specs glasses, and Meta is working on AR glasses too.
I don’t think they will transform the landscape of VR, especially when Meta itself has been divesting from VR software and largely moving on from the VR version of Horizon Worlds.

It also sounds like the next one will be something a little different.UploadVR reported that Meta's next head-worn VR device might launch in 2026, but it likely won't be a big, bulky VR headset like we're used to seeing from Quest devices.

SEE ALSO: Meta reportedly replacing human risk assessors with AI According to an older report by The Information that originally shed light on this new Meta device, codenamed "Puffin," it looks more like a pair of big glasses than a headset and weighs less than 100g.
While we’re still waiting on a precise release date, Meta did reveal an avalanche of details on the hardware alongside a slate of new immersive and casual viewing content coming to the headset.
You can catch Road to VR’s hands-on with Meta VR Glasses here .

As for sensors, VR Glasses comes with a wide array: eye-tracking cameras for UI selection and biometric unlock, front and downward-facing camera sensors for a wider hand-tracking range, and full color passthrough sensors offering 26 PPD.
It of course also does the same capable 6DOF spatial tracking pioneered in the company’s Quest lineup.
